blocking.title: Shoulder clamp jumps at the overhead HARD boundary; continuity gate fails for the shoulders
blocking.file: src/patient/JointModel.js (shoulder reference frameXY(-UP, FRONT) at line 266; limitsOf shoulder at lines 338-350)
blocking.measured: Sweeping the shoulder relative rotation in 0.25 deg steps from 170 to 190 deg: pure flexion output jumps 120.0 deg at an input of 180.25 deg (from flexion 180 to the extension limit 60); pure abduction jumps 110.0 deg (shoulder.L and shoulder.R). The swing-twist split wraps at 180 deg swing, which with the hanging-down reference is exactly the flexion and abduction HARD value, so an input 0.25 deg past overhead is read as extension or adduction near 180 deg and projected onto the 60/70 deg ellipse. In addition the twist range widens to +-180 deg between 150 and 180 deg elevation, i.e. an overhead humerus has no rotation limit. The implementer's continuity test keeps its walks within 150 deg of neutral, which excludes exactly this region. Other joints only wrap far beyond their HARD range (hip 50 deg beyond, elbow 30 deg beyond).
blocking.needed: Either doc 12's anterior reference with swing-dependent rotation limits, or a clamp that compares the candidate projections of both swing-twist representations near the wrap and keeps the one nearest the input in rotation angle; and a bounded humeral rotation above 150 deg elevation. Then a continuity test that crosses the 180 deg wrap of every joint.

blocking.title: SupportSurface.sd (and skinPenetration) under-reads how deep skin is below a pad top; its direction points down for deep points
blocking.measured: The pads are 75 mm thick plain boxes (y 0.8775-0.9525). A box SDF gives the distance to the NEAREST face, so a vertex more than 37.5 mm below the top reads its distance to the pad's bottom face. On today's rest pose the calves/heels lie 51.8 mm below the leg-pad tops (independent depth below the drawn top, 2,755 vertices deeper than 2 mm), but SupportSurface.sd reads them as 23.2 mm; 283 vertices are under-read by more than 10 mm; skinPenetration().supportMaxMm reports 37.5 mm (owner was told 'up to 37.5 mm into the pads'). For such points the sd gradient points down, so the G3 hard-constraint pass (§4.6 step 3, 'move T out along the contact normals') would push them out through the bottom of the pad.
blocking.evidence: probe/sd-probe-chrome.json; probe/probe-*.json independent.penetration (51.8 mm in Chrome and WebKit, both sizes)
blocking.needed: For resting surfaces, measure and constrain the depth below the top inside the footprint (one-sided support: box extended downward, or use supportAt), and report max/p95 on that; keep the SDF only for side contact with rails and fittings.
